video.title: Charlotte Hornets Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]

summary: Josh Lloyd previews the Charlotte Hornets for the 2026/27 fantasy season. He starts with the trade that sent Buddy Hield to Chicago for Rob Dillingham, which he calls a move to save money. His main question is how the team runs without LaMelo Ball, since Coby White, Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel will have to split the ball handling. His projected starters are Coby White, Kon Knueppel, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid and Moussa Diabaté. Grayson Allen is the likely sixth man and fills in while Knueppel's hamstring heals. He sees White, Reid and Miller as under-drafted, calls Knueppel his biggest fade (keep him out of the top 50; the 60s is fair), names Allen as his late-round swing, and names the rookie taken 14th (resolved here as Hannes Steinbach) as a stash for deep leagues. Last, he covers injury updates and the schedule: 13 back-to-backs, which he says matters very little.

rules.text: Avoid drafting players who start the season injured, but the season is 25 weeks long. Do not drop a player with a short-term injury too far.
rules.quote: But the season is 25 weeks long. So, how you valued Kniple before, don't drop it too far down.

rules.text: Hamstring injuries tend to happen again. A long ruling at the start can mean the team is being careful or that the injury is serious.
rules.quote: Now, hamstrings are prone to re-injury.

rules.text: Do not judge a player only by last season's rank. Look at the context, such as injuries, minutes limits and role.
rules.quote: take off the single season blinkers because there are plenty of reasons for this.

rules.text: Do not boost a fill-in starter much because of a short injury to a starter. The injury may last only a few games or none.
rules.quote: just because Knippel may miss one or two games, I don't think you need to go crazy on grabbing Grayson Allen.

rules.text: Players on teams nobody pays attention to often get overlooked in drafts and can be good value.
rules.quote: because they're the Hornets and no one cares about them is that a lot of their players slip through the cracks.

rules.text: Stash candidates fit weekly lock leagues, games-cap formats and deep-bench leagues. In 16-team leagues, draft promising rookies.
rules.quote: If I'm in a deep league that goes to 16 teams, I'm drafting him.

rules.text: The number of back-to-backs barely matters. The gap between 13 and 16 is about one game every two months.
rules.quote: the difference between 13 back-to-backs and 16 back-to-backs over the course of a season is three.

rules.text: Be careful with auction mock drafts. The information from them can mislead more than it helps.
rules.quote: it has a lot of information that can be misleading versus being helpful.

team_notes.text: Projected starters: White, Knueppel, Miller, Reid and Diabaté. Allen starts while Knueppel is out. Bench: Allen, Schröder, Steinbach, O'Neale and Grant Williams.

team_notes.text: Schedule: 4-3-4 for a March 28 end date and 3-4-4 for Yahoo's April 4 default. Only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
team_notes.quote: their schedule is 4-3-4, that's one away from the max.
